jobs.title: Senior Manager, Corporate Strategy
jobs.description:
Founded in 1986, Westlake Corporation (NYSE: WLK) is a Fortune 500 global diversified industrial company that manufactures and supplies essential products that enhance the daily lives of people around the globe. Our products are used in housing and infrastructure, packaging and healthcare, and automotive and consumer goods.

SUMMARY
As Senior Manager – Corporate Strategy you will play a crucial role in regularly partnering and engaging with executive leadership team, business unit leadership and other stakeholders to shape strategic direction, drive portfolio-level initiatives, navigate complex business environments and build disciplined strategy execution capabilities across the organization.
With approximately 8+ of relevant experience, the Senior Manager – Corporate Strategy brings deep expertise in corporate and business-unit strategy, operating model design, and the ability to effectively guide matrixed project teams to deliver desired results.

DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
May include, but are not limited to, the following:
- Strategic business planning and analysis
- Serve as a key thought partner in identifying, evaluating, and prioritizing new strategic business opportunities, with frequent exposure to and interaction with executive leadership.

- Develop and deliver insightful market, competitive, and financial analyses to inform short- and long-term strategic planning; translate findings into clear recommendations for senior leadership.

- Develop robust business cases and financial models, including scenario analysis and forecasts, evaluate strategic options, quantify value creation, and support investment decisions.

- Monitor performance of strategic initiatives against targets; track KPIs, identify risks and variances, and recommend corrective actions to ensure expected outcomes are achieved.

- Market entry, business development, and corporate development
- Systematically scan, identify, and assess organic and inorganic growth opportunities by business, geography, and region, ensuring alignment with the enterprise strategic plan and portfolio priorities.

- Conduct rigorous, fact-based analysis of market trends, customer requirements, competitive dynamics, regulatory developments, technology advancements, and new product innovations.

- Support corporate development efforts including target screening, due diligence, deal structuring, partnerships, and post-merger integration.

- Business transformation
- Partner with business leaders and Project Managers to scope, design, and execute large-scale transformation initiatives that align with the strategic plan and deliver measurable business outcomes.

- Apply disciplined project and program management practices to develop charters, detailed project plans, timelines, resource plans, and risk/issue logs; track progress against milestones and escalate concerns as needed.

- Develop compelling written communications (white-papers, PowerPoint) to gain alignment and approval from C-suite

EDUCATION, EXPERIENCE AND QUALIFICATIONS
- Bachelor’s degree in Business, Economics, Finance, Engineering, or related field required.

- Advanced degree (MBA or related) preferred but not required.

- 8+ years of relevant professional experience, with a significant portion in management consulting, corporate strategy, or strategic planning.

- Strong executive presence and communication skills—able to distill complex ideas into concise, compelling narratives and present recommendations in an executive setting.

- Demonstrated track record leading complex, multi-stakeholder strategy projects from conception through execution, manage multiple priorities, and deliver high-quality work under tight timelines.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to sit; stand; walk; use hands to touch, handle, or feel; reach with hands and arms; and talk or hear. The employee is occasionally required to stoop, kneel, or crouch. The employee must regularly lift and/or move up to 5 pounds, frequently lift and/or move up to 10 pounds, and occasionally lift and/or move up to 15 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus. jobs.title: Senior Director, Financial Planning & Analysis
jobs.description:
The Senior Director, FP&A leads corporate financial planning and analysis activities across Westlake, with responsibility for enterprise-level FP&A deliverables and for partnering with segment and business unit finance teams (e.g., Performance & Essential Materials and Housing & Infrastructure Products segments). The incumbent serves as a key strategic finance leader and business partner to executive leadership, shaping Westlake’s financial plans in support of its long-term strategy and capital deployment priorities.

This role is accountable for driving an integrated, disciplined budgeting and target-setting process across the enterprise. The Senior Director, FP&A works closely with segment and business unit leaders to translate strategic and operational plans into clear financial targets, challenge underlying assumptions, and establish robust cost and productivity objectives. Through enhanced budget frameworks, standardized methodologies, and transparent performance dashboards, the incumbent increases ownership and accountability for results, improves cost visibility and accountability, and enables proactive cost management and margin optimization.

The Senior Director, FP&A also leads the development and continuous improvement of Westlake’s enterprise forecasting capabilities. This includes designing and refining driver-based forecasting models, coordinating regular forecast cycles with segment and business unit finance teams, identifying and implementing technological solutions to improve efficiency and effectiveness in the FP&A process, and implementing scenario and sensitivity analyses to assess the impact of market conditions, commodity price movements, and operational initiatives on earnings and cash flow. The incumbent plays a central role in supporting more accurate, insight-driven earnings guidance by ensuring forecasts are analytically rigorous, aligned with business realities, and effectively synthesized for the Executive Management team and other key stakeholders. Strong communication and collaboration skills are necessary.

- Lead the development of short- and long-range strategic plans at the corporate level, integrating inputs from segments and businesses and reflecting market, macroeconomic, and industry specific dynamics.

- Research and interpret relevant market, societal, and macroeconomic trends; incorporate insights into forecasts, strategic plans, and executive briefings.

jobs.title: Vice President and Treasurer
jobs.description:
SUMMARY
The Vice President & Treasurer is responsible for leading Westlake’s global treasury function, including corporate and project finance, liquidity and cash management, capital markets, foreign exchange, credit and risk management. This role ensures appropriate returns for financial risks retained by the company and secures cost-effective funding to support operations and growth, while maintaining flexible access to global sources of capital and insurance.

The Vice President & Treasurer also serves as a key strategic advisor, providing economic, financial and business counsel in support of operational decisions, mergers and acquisitions, and other strategic initiatives and special projects.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
- Lead and maintain an efficient global cash and liquidity management framework, ensuring strong relationships with creditworthy banking partners at competitive cost.

- Ensure operational liquidity to meet obligations on a timely basis while minimizing short-term borrowing costs and achieving investment returns consistent with preservation of principal, including ownership of 13 week cash forecasting

- Evaluate and execute long-term debt financing in support of strategic and operational growth at or below market cost, with attention to covenant flexibility and overall capital structure optimization.

- Structure and arrange project financings that appropriately transfer operational or financial risk to third parties at competitive pricing.

- Manage the company’s exposure to interest rate, foreign exchange and other financial market risks through use of fixed rate indebtedness, derivatives and foreign exchange markets, in alignment with corporate risk management policies.

- Ownership of cost of capital calculations utilized for returns across the enterprise

- Protect Westlake from catastrophic loss through effective loss control and risk mitigation measures, cost-effective purchase of insurance, robust claims administration and ongoing review of risk retention levels as exposures evolve, including leadership of global enterprise risk management program

- Support product sales through effective global credit management, including credit policies and procedures, customer credit analysis and limits, collections and dispute resolution, and portfolio-level credit risk monitoring.

- Manage and cultivate relationships with investment banks, commercial banks, rating agencies and economic advisors, providing market intelligence and access that support the development of Westlake’s strategic plan and opportunistic transactions.

- Support the CEO, CFO, business units and business development in identifying and evaluating acquisition, divestiture and strategic partnership opportunities.

- Assist the Chairman’s office, CEO and business units in the development and refinement of strategic plans by providing economic and financial guidelines and scenario analyses, and delivering analytical insight and recommendations on value creation and capital allocation.

- Provide leadership, direction and oversight for treasury-related policies, processes, systems and controls globally.

- Champion continuous improvement and operational excellence within the Treasury function.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES
- Provide leadership and direction to the Treasury department, including cash management, capital markets, risk management and credit teams.

- Responsible for staffing, performance management, coaching and development, and succession planning within the Treasury function.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE
- Bachelor’s degree in Business, Accounting, Finance or related field required; MBA or equivalent advanced degree strongly preferred.

- Minimum of 10 years of progressively responsible experience in corporate finance, project finance, capital markets and/or credit management, including at least 5 years in a leadership role managing professional staff.

- Deep knowledge of corporate finance theory and practice, investment theory and fixed income mathematics, and capital markets instruments and structures.

- Experience analyzing customer credit risk and designing solutions to mitigate risks associated with extension of credit and trade finance.

- Strong working knowledge of financial accounting, financial statement analysis and key performance metrics.
